significance.quote: We observe this process at a 6.7-sigma confidence level

summary.plain: COHERENT reports observing neutrinos scatter off entire atomic nuclei at once, a process the paper says had evaded experimental demonstration for forty-three years after its first theoretical description. The detector was a 14.6-kilogram caesium-iodide crystal at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge.
summary.technical: Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) at a 6.7σ confidence level, using a 14.6 kg CsI[Na] scintillator exposed to the neutrino emissions from the SNS; the characteristic energy and time signatures predicted by the Standard Model are observed in high signal-to-background conditions, and improved constraints on non-standard neutrino interactions with quarks are derived.

title: Observation of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
why_it_matters: The abstract says the predicted cross section is the largest by far of all low-energy neutrino couplings, yet the process had eluded detection for four decades; it adds that the interaction offers new opportunities to study neutrino properties and leads to a miniaturization of detector size, with potential technological applications. The paper notes that WIMP direct-detection searches rely on the same coherent enhancement.
